Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: STP was among ten African countries to benefit from AfDB digital trade and digital payments project (2023). E-Signature Law was passed (documented in April 2025 World Bank ISR). However, no documented operational integration of national payment systems with a data exchange platform.
revision_notes: Both originally cited sources were fetched and are genuine and relevant. The World Bank Digital STP Implementation Status Report (archived 11 Apr 2025) confirms the government has completed an ID management pilot and 'is looking to implement a digital ID, as well as a government-wide data exchange layer' -- i.e. the data exchange layer itself remains at the planning stage, with no evidence of any payment-system integration into it yet. The Biometric Update piece (Jun 2025) corroborates that digital ID/data exchange work is still at pilot stage with no fixed rollout timeline. Checked the AfDB-cited project directly: it is the Institutional Support for Digital Payments and e-Commerce Policies for Cross-Border Trade (IDECT) project (2023), which is a policy/capacity-building initiative for cross-border e-payments, not a domestic G2P/G2B data-exchange integration -- the original comment's framing overstates its relevance somewhat, but this does not change the score. A separate national retail payment system (Dobra24/SICOI, modernised with SIBS technology from 2021) exists and is regulated by the central bank, but no source shows it connected to a government data exchange for G2P/G2B transactions. Score of 2 (Planned) is confirmed: a data exchange layer is explicitly planned per the 2025 World Bank document, but payments integration into it is not yet under development.
revised_comments: São Tomé and Príncipe has a functioning national retail payment system (Dobra24/SICOI, modernised via a SIBS-built platform from 2021) regulated by the Central Bank (BCSTP), but this is not yet integrated with a government-wide data exchange for government-to-person (G2P) or government-to-business (G2B) transactions. The World Bank-financed Digital São Tomé and Príncipe project reports that, following completion of a digital ID pilot, government is now looking to implement both a digital ID and a government-wide data exchange layer, indicating the integration remains at the planning stage. São Tomé and Príncipe also participates in the AfDB/Smart Africa Institutional Support for Digital Payments and e-Commerce Policies for Cross-Border Trade project (2023), which supports policy development for cross-border e-payments rather than domestic G2P/G2B integration.
